findings.evidence: field_is_sensitive({'type':'text','name':n,'value':'482913'}) is False for emailverificationcode, mfacode, onetimecode, twofactorcode, 2facode, tfacode, authenticatorcode, authenticationcode, onetimepin, smspin, cardcode and cardverificationcode (also False with value '123'), and for authtoken, accesstoken, clientsecret and secretkey. \bverification ?code\b and \bone ?time\b need a word boundary that a prefix removes; _CODE_LABEL (\bcode\b) misses run-together '...code'; RUN_TOGETHER enumerates prefixes. Real Chromium (tests/assist/fixtures/run_snapshot.cjs on /tmp/uri_review_R3/leak.html) returned sensitive:false with values 482913/551203/660114/737/884205/9152 for emailverificationcode/mfacode/onetimecode/cardcode/twofactorcode/onetimepin. Feeding that snapshot through AssistCommands (FakeAdapter, FakeClient) and assist_ask put all six values into the Brain request body (/tmp/uri_review_R3/e2e_leak.py). findings.suggested_fix: Stop enumerating prefixes. In both layers: match otp|mfa|2fa|onetime|twofactor|verification|authenticat|cvv|cvc|token|secret as substrings of the joined word; treat a short all-digit value as a code when any name, label or placeholder word ENDS with code or pin (keeping the postal/zip/pincode/country/area exclusions); keep the JS pattern byte-identical to Python. Add these names to tricky_fields.html and the parity test, and correct the AC7 row.

findings.evidence: check_address('64:ff9b:1:a00:0:100:808:808') is allowed: the last 32 bits are 8.8.8.8. Under RFC 6052/8215 a /48-prefix translator reads the embedded IPv4 from bits 48-63 and 72-87, which gives 10.0.0.1. The return at line 75 bypasses the flags check, although Python marks 64:ff9b:1::/48 as non-global. Exploiting it needs a local RFC 8215 NAT64 with a non-/96 prefix and an attacker-controlled AAAA record.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse 64:ff9b:1::/48 outright, or check the embedded IPv4 at every RFC 6052 prefix-length position.
findings.title: The NAT64 local-use prefix 64:ff9b:1::/48 is assumed to embed IPv4 in the last 32 bits, and its early return skips the is_global check

findings.evidence: The worker comment says 'Both yield the single Brain slot to the user's turn', but oi_turn calls only assist.cancel_brain_work('user_turn'). WebResearch._guarded_complete checks brain_idle once before the call; make_complete then runs client.complete_json(timeout_s=60) with no cancel token. On the -np 1 runtime a user turn can queue behind it for up to 60 s.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the web synthesis call a cancel token and cancel it on oi_turn, as Assist does, or correct the comment and document the delay.
findings.title: Web research Brain synthesis does not yield to a user turn that starts during it; the worker cancels only Assist
